title: Text Processing Decisions: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Text Processing Decisions: Visual Guide

1. Who Makes The Keys | three documents saying CloudRun, Cloud Run and cloud-run, with lowercase / punctuation-split / subtoken toggles and a query analyzer that can be left out of step, showing the dictionary, the postings lists and the Boolean intersection | the inverted index from lesson 01 can only retrieve the keys its analyzer created, and the index-time and query-time analyzers are one contract that must match or the postings list comes back empty

2. Stemming's Two Errors | the corpus d1 connection timeout, d2 connected clients, d3 connective tissue under no stemming / Porter-style / broad connect*, judged against a networking or a biomedical collection, with live precision, recall, F1 and the key's df and idf | stemming buys recall by merging postings and spends precision by merging concepts, understemming misses d2 and overstemming admits d3, and merging forms raises df so idf log10(3/df) falls 0.48 to 0.18 to 0 and the term stops discriminating

3. Stop Words And Positions | the text state of the art with stop words kept, removed with renumbered positions, or removed with gaps preserved, three phrase queries checked against those positions, plus a slider for the document frequency of the in a 100-million-document corpus | removal saves postings and destroys phrase, name and citation queries irreversibly, renumbering positions manufactures a phrase nobody wrote, and correct position increments limit the damage without restoring the terms

4. Folding Into Classes | nine surface forms including composed and combining-mark Résumé, full-width Latin, café and US versus us, run through toggleable Unicode NFC, case folding, naive accent folding and NFKC, grouped into live equivalence classes with flags for useful and destructive merges | normalization is valuable precisely because it discards distinctions, so order matters (naive accent folding cannot see a decomposed accent until NFC runs), meaning-bearing case and accents need an exact field alongside the folded one, and the rules must be identical and versioned at index and query time

5. The Analyzer Contract | one global aggressiveness slider from raw tokens through case folding, accent folding, stop-word removal and stemming, scored against seven query classes at once, with a toggle that adds an exact unfolded field and a reindex badge | no single global setting serves every query class, so the conflict is a field-design problem rather than a tuning problem: a second exact field recovers precision failures but never recall ones, and any equivalence change means a full reindex and per-class evaluation
